title: Alaçatı & Çeşme Guide: Windsurfing, Stone Hotels & Aegean Dining

metaDescription: Alaçatı & Çeşme guide covering İzmir Airport transfers, Meltemi windsurfing vs calm beaches, spring/autumn stone hotels, and Urla wine pairings.
quickAnswer: Alaçatı sits just 85 kilometers (50–65 minutes) west of İzmir Airport (ADB), making it Türkiye's easiest Aegean escape. Visit June through August for peak Meltemi windsurfing, or pick May, September, and October for calmer swimming at Ilıca and Boyalık, quieter stone boutique hotels, and a 35-minute drive to Urla's Michelin-recognized wineries and dining rooms.

body.text: This alacati cesme guide separates the real Çeşme Peninsula from peak-August weekend gridlock. Alaçatı's restored Greek-era limestone lanes, Çeşme's thermal-fed turquoise bays, and neighboring Urla's vineyard kitchens form one of the sharpest culinary-and-coast pairings in western Türkiye—provided you match your timing to the wind and weekend crowds.
How far is Alaçatı from İzmir Airport?

Direct Answer: Alaçatı is roughly 85 kilometers west of İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport (ADB) via the smooth O-32/E87 toll motorway, taking 50 to 65 minutes by private car or rental vehicle in normal traffic (up to 75 minutes on peak summer Friday evenings). Year-round Havaş airport coaches also link ADB directly to Alaçatı and Çeşme in about 75 minutes.

Private transfers or rental cars cover the [85-kilometer motorway run in 50 to 65 minutes](https://utopiaizmirtransfer.com/en/blog/alacati-transfer-from-izmir-airport/), exiting straight onto the peninsula without entering downtown İzmir. If you are traveling solo or without a car, the [Havaş airport coach](https://likecesme.com/bus-havas/) runs year-round via Urla for [approximately 550 TL per passenger](https://www.izmirvipairporttransfer.com/blog-yazilari/11-how-to-get-from-alacati-to-adnan-menderes-airport), dropping you near Alaçatı's main interchange where local taxis wait.
When is the best month for windsurfing vs calm beaches?

Direct Answer: June, July, and August deliver the strongest, most reliable northern Meltemi winds for windsurfing and wingfoiling in shallow Alaçatı Bay, whereas May, late September, and October bring gentler breezes and calmer water for swimming. Even in windy midsummer, south-facing coves like Altınkum and Delikli Koy stay far more sheltered than the north shore.

body.text: Alaçatı's dedicated surf bay stays waist-deep for hundreds of meters offshore, making it ideal for beginners learning under steady [mid-May to September Meltemi winds](https://www.planetwindsurfholidays.com/resorts/turkey/alacati). Non-surfers wanting warm, glassy shallows should head ten minutes north to Ilıca Beach—where thermal springs seep into the sandy shallows—or drive west to Boyalık and Çeşme Marina.
Why are Alaçatı stone boutique hotels popular in spring and autumn?

Direct Answer: Alaçatı's restored limestone boutique hotels shine in spring and autumn because courtyard rooms stay cool without constant air conditioning, late-night street noise from Kemalpaşa Caddesi disappears, and nightly rates drop 30 to 50 percent below July–August peaks. Spring brings the April Alaçatı Herb Festival, while autumn pairs warm sea water with unhurried breakfasts.

Most historic stone houses have six to fifteen rooms wrapped around a walled citrus garden and small plunge pool. In peak August, weekend revelers from İzmir and Istanbul keep the central alleys loud past 2:00 AM. Booking in May, June, September, or October—and picking a hotel on the quieter Hacımemiş edge rather than directly on Kemalpaşa Caddesi—gives you the architecture and Aegean breakfast spreads without losing sleep.
How do you combine Alaçatı with Urla?

Direct Answer: Combine Alaçatı with Urla by spending two or three nights in Alaçatı for beaches and surf, then driving 35 to 45 minutes east along the O-32 motorway to Urla for one or two vineyard nights—or visiting Urla as a long lunch-and-tasting detour on your way back to İzmir Airport (ADB).

Urla has become Türkiye's sharpest farm-to-table hub, anchored by the [Urla Vineyard Trail (Urla Bağ Yolu)](https://www.turkish-wine.com/the-urla-vineyard-trail-urla-ba%C4%9F-yolu) and 13 restaurants recognized in the [MICHELIN Guide Urla](https://guide.michelin.com/en/tr/izmir/urla_2808630/restaurants) selection. Structure your pairing around four practical stops:

items: Book Michelin tables weeks ahead: Reserve dinner at One-Star [OD Urla](https://guide.michelin.com/en/izmir/izmir_2809416/restaurant/od-urla), Vino Locale, or Narımor—or lunch at Hiç Lokanta—well before arrival, especially for Friday and Saturday evenings.
Visit two wineries, not five: Pair a tasting at Urla Şarapçılık or USCA Winery with a slow olive-grove lunch rather than rushing through ten tasting rooms.

Sample Aegean seafood on both coasts: Combine a casual meze evening in Alaçatı or Çeşme (highlighted alongside Urla in the [MICHELIN Guide feature on Sota Alaçatı and Gula Urla](https://guide.michelin.com/en/article/travel/from-sea-to-table-sota-alacati-gula-urla)) with Urla's wood-fired inland kitchens.
Use a driver on wine days: Hiring a private driver between Alaçatı, Urla, and ADB lets everyone taste local Bornova Misketi and Urla Karası wines safely.

faq.q: Is Alaçatı or Çeşme better to stay in?
faq.a: Stay in Alaçatı if you want walkable limestone lanes, boutique courtyard hotels, and dinner on foot; stay in Çeşme, Ilıca, or Boyalık if you want direct beachfront access and larger resort pools.

faq.q: Can you take a day ferry from Çeşme to Chios, Greece?
faq.a: Yes. Regular passenger ferries cross from Çeşme port to the Greek island of Chios in roughly 30 to 45 minutes, making an easy cross-border day trip if your visa allows re-entry.

faq.q: Do I need a rental car in Alaçatı?
faq.a: A car is unnecessary inside Alaçatı village itself—which is largely pedestrian—but very useful for reaching Ilıca Beach, Alaçatı Surf Bay, Delikli Koy, and Urla's wineries.

faq.q: When is the Alaçatı Herb Festival (Ot Festivali)?
faq.a: It takes place each April (exact weekend dates are announced annually by Çeşme Municipality) and celebrates wild Aegean greens, foraging walks, and local street cooking.

faq.q: How can I combine Alaçatı with Ephesus?
faq.a: Ephesus sits about 1.5 hours southeast of Alaçatı via İzmir's ring road, so you can easily link [Ephesus and Selçuk](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/where-to-stay-for-ephesus) with two or three coastal nights in Alaçatı and Urla.

faq.q: Are Alaçatı beaches free to enter?
faq.a: Public beaches like Ilıca Public Beach and Delikli Koy are free, whereas private beach clubs along Aya Yorgi Bay and Çiftlikköy charge daily entry fees or minimum food-and-drink spends in summer.
